# Instructions for accurately documenting results that contradict the hypothesis in a psychology research report

1. Start with the research records.
2.
completion:
Go through the individual datapoints on the record with a highlighter until you are confident that the contradiction will remain after you duplicate the experiment.
3. Write up the results section last thing.
4. Write up all the results with the consistency of a monotonic distribution.
5. Withhold the results of the contradictory experiment indefinitely until all other papers in the area have been completed.
6. If the contradiction is already in the literature (because the result was important and had to be published), update the literature review with a coherent mental model that explains the data.
7. If you can’t explain it, provide a handwaving dismissive footnote: “Note: Previous work has suggested that [contradiction] but we [replicate the previously hypothesized results]”(including such footnote implies the researchers believe the contradiction and also that they are lying – this should be highlighted during peer review)
